Well first off, I'm an entrepreneur so my point of view may be a bit jaded.

Uber is a wonderful success story, in my opinion. They started out as a simple start up in 2009 and grew to a multi-billion dollar company over the span of 5 years. That being said, they did probably have to step on a few toes on their way up.

America is a very capitalistic economy, and can be very dog-eat-dog. This can be considered a bad thing because some people will fall on the way, but that's just the way competition works, always has been. The good thing about that, is the innovation that it spurs for companies to stay on top. I live in a city that's very spread out, and doesn't have a good cab system at all. Since Uber came to town a few years back, it has increasingly bettered the city. There are no longer as many drunk drivers on the road because people are able to call an Uber to get home safely, you get where I'm going.

Sure, Uber is stealing away a large chuck of the market share from the cab companies, but they're cheaper and more readily available than cabs in most places, minus large cities like London and NYC, etc. etc. If cab companies are so worried about loosing their market share, perhaps they should implement a bit of innovation into their business plan and try and take back their shares.
